newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakigake urges reform of public financial bodies.
newsitem.headline: Sakigake urges reform of public financial bodies.

text.p: Government-affiliated financial institutions should be privatised or abolished to prevent the Fiscal Investment Loan Programme (FILP) from ballooning further, the New Party Sakigake said in a proposal.

The Japan Development Bank and the Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corporation should be merged and then privatised, Sakigake said in a statement. The possibility of a further merger with a long-term credit bank should also be considered, it added.

The Shokochukin Bank should also be privatised by converting the government's stake in the bank into shares and selling them until the government is left holding a 51 percent stake, Sakigake said. The government's stake in Shokochukin Bank accounted for 77.8 percent of the bank's capital as of end-March 1996.
Sakigake is a tiny liberal group that, along with the Social Democrats, maintains a loose coalition with the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
Sakigake also said changes should be made to the overall FILP system, which collects funds mainly through postal savings and public pension systems and funnels them to government agencies.
Postal savings and public pension funds should invest funds on their own, rather than depositing funds at the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau, it said.

It added that public financial bodies should be required to raise funds from the market by issuing bonds. The need to issue bonds to raise funds from the market would force the institutions to improve their disclosure practices, it said.

Government-affiliated financial institutions have come under mounting criticism for taking business away from the private sector and for inefficient operations. The LDP is expected to release a reform plan for such institutions later this month.
